messages:
tanya_docs: heads-up: i'm drafting a short migration note for customers moving from the legacy global TTL to per-tenant retention. i want to include a tiny example showing a bulk 'place on hold' call (so customers can preserve a set of entries during legal migration). want to keep tone clear and avoid implying permanence. @mike_infra @lee_security any red flags?

mike_infra: fine from infra side. couple caveats: (1) bulk operations are rate-limited so add a note to batch by tenant; (2) holds pause TTL-based purges but do not change storage tier or lifetime planning for backups.

lee_security: add a sentence that holds are recorded in the audit trail (who/when) and that held items remain subject to encryption policies (customer KMS if enabled). avoid words like 'undeletable'.

nora_compliance: from compliance: call out that holds are administrative actions and require the `audit:hold` RBAC permission; also note that legal holds should be scoped narrowly where possible. include internal SOC2 appendix link.

sam_eng: i can write a minimal curl + py snippet for bulk hold. suggest endpoint `POST /v1/audit/holds/bulk` with body {"log_ids": [...], "reason": "migration"}. response will be 202 Accepted if queued. i'll keep examples safe for public docs (no fragile headers).

mike_infra: add an example response showing 202 + job id, and a note: "check job status via GET /v1/audit/holds/jobs/:id". include warning: "large batches may be processed asynchronously".

 tanya_docs: draft language i plan to add: 

"Quick migration note: If you need to preserve multiple audit entries while migrating retention configuration, you can place them on legal hold in bulk. Placing entries on hold pauses automatic TTL deletion for those entries until the hold is removed by an authorized user. Holds are auditable actions and will be recorded with the actor and timestamp. When customer-managed KMS is enabled, held entries are encrypted with the customer's key while preserved."

Examples (public-friendly):

curl example (bulk hold request):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds/bulk \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"log_ids": ["l-1001","l-1002","l-1003"], "reason": "retention migration - 2026"}'
```

python example (async job response):
```
# python (requests)
import requests
r = requests.post(
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/holds/bulk",
  headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"},
  json={"log_ids": ["l-1001","l-1002"], "reason": "retention migration"}
)
print(r.status_code)  # 202
print(r.json())       # {"job_id": "job-abc123", "status": "queued"}
```

notes: requires `audit:hold` permission. Bulk calls may return 202 Accepted and process asynchronously; poll the job status endpoint to confirm completion. Held items bypass configured TTL purges but remain subject to existing retention obligations and encryption policies. Large batches should be split to avoid hitting rate limits.

lee_security: nit: say "pause TTL-based purges" and include parenthetical: "(does not change backup lifecycle)". Also prefer we avoid exposing exact job id format in public docs.

nora_compliance: LGTM with that tweak; add link to SOC2 retention appendix: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/soc2#retention. also remind readers that removal of holds is also auditable and should follow organizational policy.

sam_eng: i'll push the snippets to PR branch 'docs/retention-migration-bulk-hold' and include a tiny example for checking job status.

docs-bot: PR 4230 opened: branch docs/retention-migration-bulk-hold. CI: linkcheck running.

 tanya_docs: thanks everyone 60a i'll merge after linkcheck. i'll also add a short troubleshooting note: if job fails with 429, retry with smaller batches and exponential backoff.
